approvalRequirements: Own an eligible newly constructed or substantially renovated nonresidential or multifamily building of at least 10,000 square feet that satisfies the County Code occupancy and timing rules.
Obtain a Department of Permitting Services certification issued within the past year showing at least 10 percent energy performance above the building code in effect when applying.
Submit the owner application in the form prescribed by the Montgomery County Department of Finance.
For a sustainability add-on, first receive the energy-reduction credit and document an eligible current green-building certification within two years after the use-and-occupancy permit.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current County Code directs the Finance Director to allow the formula-based credit for an eligible building that satisfies the certification and application rules. The credit is not competitively ranked and is limited by the statutory calculation and the building's property-tax liability.
reviews.evidenceText: Current County Code section 52-103B requires a recent permitting certification, at least 10 percent above-code energy performance, a Finance application, and prior approval of the energy-reduction credit before any sustainability add-on. The Director must allow the calculated credit for eligible years.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Moorhead Public Service business customer and install the measure at a qualifying served facility.
Select equipment or a project that meets the current Bright Energy Solutions measure-specific technical requirements.
Obtain advance review or preapproval for custom, electrification, or other projects for which the current application requires it.
Submit the applicable application with invoices, equipment specifications, project data, and any requested savings documentation.
Permit program inspection or verification and remain within current incentive caps and available funding.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Moorhead Public Service currently participates in Bright Energy Solutions and offers published business rebates across the mapped efficiency categories. These incentives are generally rule-based rather than competitively scored, so a qualifying and documented project is likely to be paid after any required preapproval and verification.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Moorhead Public Service member page lists 2026 business rebates and directs customers to complete and submit the applicable Bright Energy Solutions forms. Custom and specialized projects remain subject to project review and approval.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Massachusetts individual, business, nonprofit, or public entity under the applicable MOR-EV vehicle category.
Purchase or lease an eligible vehicle through an authorized pathway and satisfy the applicable purchase-price, use, registration, and retention rules.
Use point-of-sale processing or submit a complete post-purchase application within the applicable filing period, including the 90-day deadline where required.
Provide purchase or lease documents, registration and residency or business records, and any income or organizational documentation required for the selected rebate.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: MOR-EV is an active vehicle-purchase and vehicle-lease rebate program. It does not award a standalone incentive for the mapped stationary fuel-cell system or EV charger installation, so the mapped retrofit is unlikely to receive an award from this opportunity.
reviews.evidenceText: Current MOR-EV materials define rebates for eligible electric and fuel-cell vehicle acquisitions, with point-of-sale or timely post-purchase documentation. They do not establish a separate capital award for charger installation or a stationary fuel-cell system.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Massachusetts applicant acquiring a qualifying new electric or fuel-cell truck under the applicable MOR-EV Trucks class category.
For a qualifying Class 2 pickup, complete the required post-purchase application within the applicable deadline.
For a qualifying Class 3 through 8 truck, obtain the required voucher or reservation before vehicle delivery and complete the claim process after acquisition.
Submit vehicle purchase, title, registration, applicant, and any fleet or operational records required by the current program rules.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current MOR-EV Trucks benefit applies to acquisition of eligible trucks, including battery-electric and fuel-cell vehicles. It does not provide a separate award for the mapped stationary fuel-cell system or EV charger installation, making an award for the mapped retrofit unlikely.
reviews.evidenceText: Current program pages distinguish a post-purchase Class 2 pickup rebate from the advance voucher process for Class 3 through 8 trucks. The incentive is tied to truck acquisition rather than standalone charging or stationary fuel-cell infrastructure.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Mora Municipal Utilities commercial or industrial customer and install the project at the served location.
Use a current 2026 business rebate form and install equipment that meets the measure-specific efficiency and technical requirements.
Obtain advance approval for a custom or non-prescriptive project when required by the applicable program form.
Submit the completed application with paid invoices, model information, contractor records, and any requested calculations or supporting documentation.
Allow verification or inspection and remain within program limits and available funding.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Mora's current municipal-utility page publishes 2026 business rebate forms for multiple mapped measures. These are generally prescriptive or project-reviewed incentives rather than competitive grants, so a compliant and documented project is likely to receive the applicable rebate.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Mora member page provides 2026 business rebate applications for lighting, heating and cooling, refrigeration, motors, compressed air, custom projects, and related efficiency measures.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Mora Municipal Utilities residential customer and install or purchase the qualifying measure for the served home.
Use the current 2026 residential rebate application and satisfy the product, efficiency, installation, and customer requirements for the selected measure.
Submit the completed claim with paid proof of purchase, model or serial information, and any measure-specific contractor or installation documentation.
Allow program verification and remain within current per-customer limits and available funding.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Mora currently publishes residential rebate forms covering several mapped HVAC, water-heating, appliance, and EV-charging measures. A qualifying claim is generally administrative rather than competitive, making payment likely after documentation review.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Mora page links 2026 residential rebates for heating and cooling, water heating, appliances, EV chargers, and other qualifying products and equipment.

approvalRequirements: Be a Morgan County REA member and install the qualifying equipment at a location served by the cooperative.
Purchase and install a measure listed in the current rebate guide and satisfy its efficiency, sizing, and installation specifications.
Submit the current application within 90 days of purchase or installation, as applicable.
Provide a dated invoice or bill of sale, model information, and any other measure-specific records requested by the cooperative.
Permit inspection or verification and remain within annual program limits and available funds.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Morgan County REA maintains current member rebates with published eligibility and documentation rules. The program is not competitively ranked, so an eligible measure filed within the stated period is likely to receive the applicable credit or rebate.
reviews.evidenceText: The current cooperative page provides the 2026 rebate guide and requires qualifying equipment on Morgan County REA lines, a timely application, and dated purchase or installation documentation.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Mountain Parks Electric member participating in the Clean Power Program.
Install a qualifying member-owned renewable generation system within the current size and equipment rules, including an eligible rooftop solar photovoltaic system.
Complete the utility interconnection process and obtain required inspection or permission to operate before claiming the rebate.
Submit the current rebate application with the final invoice, system information, production estimate, and other required records within the program filing period.
Comply with the one-rebate and current funding limitations.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Mountain Parks Electric currently offers a fixed Clean Power Program rebate for qualifying interconnected renewable systems. A member whose rooftop solar project completes interconnection and submits the required records is likely to receive the rebate while funds remain; an energy-monitoring system by itself is not the funded measure.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Mountain Parks Electric materials describe a member renewable-system rebate that follows interconnection and inspection and requires a timely application, invoice, and system-production documentation.

approvalRequirements: Be a Mountain View Electric Association member and install the qualifying equipment at the member's served property.
Purchase a new product or complete a project included in the current 2026 rebate guide and satisfy its technical requirements.
Pay the eligible out-of-pocket project cost and submit the online rebate application within 90 days of purchase or installation.
Provide an itemized receipt or invoice, manufacturer and model information, and any measure-specific installation records.
Allow program verification and comply with current rebate caps and funding availability.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: MVEA currently offers published member rebates across multiple mapped heat-pump, HVAC, appliance, EV-charging, and related categories. These are formula-based bill credits rather than competitive awards, so a timely qualifying claim is likely to be approved.
reviews.evidenceText: The current MVEA rebate pages require member eligibility, qualifying new equipment, paid project costs, an application within 90 days, and itemized product documentation before a bill credit is issued.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Silicon Valley Power multifamily customer with a gas boiler serving at least 25 individually metered dwelling units.
Propose an approved all-electric replacement that meets the named pilot's equipment and project requirements.
Submit detailed gas and electric scopes, itemized quotes, a project schedule, greenhouse-gas and energy-impact calculations, and major equipment specifications.
Complete pre-installation inspection and obtain written SVP approval before installation, then complete post-installation inspection and final invoice review.
Remain within the named pilot's first-come participant and budget limits.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The named Multifamily Boiler Electrification Pilot was a 2025-2026, July-through-June limited pilot and is no longer listed on SVP's current electrification page. A separate current Customer Directed Electrification Rebate may support a similar project, but that does not make a new award under the named pilot likely.
reviews.evidenceText: The named application identifies a 2025-2026 limited pilot with a July-through-June budget, first-come enrollment, and extensive preapproval requirements. SVP's current page lists the broader Customer Directed Electrification Rebate instead of the named pilot.

approvalRequirements: Own or manage an eligible Oregon multifamily property in participating utility territory and use the correct current pathway for the building size and project area.
Install a measure that meets the current 2026 Energy Trust technical, customer, and contractor requirements.
Obtain advance review or reservation for any measure or custom project for which the current program requires preapproval.
Submit the applicable incentive application with invoices, equipment specifications, contractor records, and other measure-specific documentation.
Complete any required inspection, savings verification, or account-manager review.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Energy Trust continues to offer active 2026 multifamily incentives, although smaller properties and larger or common-area projects now follow different delivery paths. The incentives are generally prescriptive or technically reviewed rather than competitive, so a qualifying project is likely to be paid after the correct pathway and documentation are used.
reviews.evidenceText: Current 2026 materials retain multifamily cash incentives but route two-to-four-unit properties and larger multifamily or common-area projects through different program channels. Measure eligibility, documentation, and any required preapproval still govern payment.

approvalRequirements: Propose eligible pre-development work for a qualifying multifamily property with at least five units or another eligible nonprofit- or municipal-owned building.
Include at least one independent qualified energy consultant or design professional on the project team.
Submit the initial intake with project details and basic financial information, then submit a full application if invited after eligibility review.
Provide the project, borrower, ownership, financial, professional-team, and pre-development cost records required for underwriting.
Receive credit approval and satisfy final loan terms and closing conditions after the product becomes available again.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: IPC's current product page states that prospective borrowers will be notified when Navigator becomes available again. Even after reopening, funding is a loan subject to project screening and credit approval, so a current new award is unlikely.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Navigator page describes eligible five-plus-unit and other qualifying buildings, a two-step intake and full-application process, a qualified professional requirement, and credit underwriting, but states that the product is not presently available.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Pennsylvania local government that was not eligible for a direct federal Energy Efficiency and Conservation Block Grant allocation.
For the active loan, have a completed Level 2 commercial energy audit and an energy-conservation-measure project design or scope.
Submit the project and borrower application to the National Energy Improvement Fund and satisfy credit, repayment, project, and funding review.
Use loan proceeds for an eligible energy-efficiency upgrade, building retrofit, or qualifying renewable project paired with efficiency measures.
Obtain Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development approval under the Local Government Unit Debt Act before loan closing.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The grant component that could fund a Level 2 energy audit is closed and may not have another round. The loan remains open while funds are available, but the audit is a prerequisite rather than an eligible standalone loan use, so the mapped audit is unlikely to receive a current award from this opportunity.
reviews.evidenceText: Pennsylvania's current page says the MORE Grant application is closed, while MORE Loans remain open while funds last. A Level 2 audit and project scope are required before applying for the loan, and DCED debt approval is required before closing.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Muscatine Power and Water commercial or industrial electric customer and install the measure at the served facility.
Choose a current qualifying commercial measure and satisfy its equipment, efficiency, sizing, and installation requirements.
Obtain advance project review for a custom measure or another project when required by the applicable program instructions.
Submit the current application with account information, final paid invoices, equipment specifications, and any requested project or savings documentation.
Permit inspection or verification and remain within current caps and available funding.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: MPW currently publishes commercial rebates for lighting, HVAC, drives, custom equipment, EV charging, and other mapped measures. These are generally prescriptive or project-reviewed incentives, so a qualifying documented project is likely to receive the applicable rebate.
reviews.evidenceText: MPW's current electric-rebate pages list active commercial measure applications and require customer eligibility, qualifying equipment, supporting invoices and specifications, and project review for custom work.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Muscatine Power and Water residential electric customer and install the qualifying measure at the served home.
Purchase and install a product or system included in the current residential rebate offering and satisfy its efficiency and installation requirements.
Submit the current residential rebate application with the paid invoice or receipt, model information, and any required contractor or certification records.
Allow program review or verification and comply with current customer and measure limits.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: MPW maintains active residential rebates for multiple mapped HVAC, water-heating, appliance, envelope, and related measures. A qualifying claim is not competitively ranked and is likely to be approved after routine documentation review.
reviews.evidenceText: Current MPW materials provide a residential rebate pathway for qualifying equipment and require a customer application with purchase, model, and installation documentation.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible applicant proposing a publicly accessible high-powered DC fast-charging site covered by the active California NEVI solicitation.
Locate the project on an eligible corridor or site and meet federal and state connector, power, payment, uptime, networking, accessibility, and public-access standards.
Coordinate with SDG&E and obtain the required utility verification, service-planning, load, and interconnection information.

Submit a complete application through the California Energy Commission system by the current deadline with site control, environmental, technical, schedule, budget, match, and commitment documentation.
Receive competitive selection and execute the grant agreement before incurring costs that require prior authorization or reimbursement eligibility.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: California's current NEVI round is an active competitive grant solicitation rather than an entitlement. A compliant SDG&E-area project can be selected, but award depends on comparative scoring, corridor and site priorities, readiness, match, and available funds.
reviews.evidenceText: The active California NEVI solicitation accepts competitive applications through October 16, 2026 for qualifying public DC fast-charging projects. Applicants need a complete technical and financial package plus utility coordination and verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible National Fuel nonresidential natural-gas customer in the Western New York program territory and complete the project at an existing facility.
Install a current qualifying natural-gas efficiency measure that meets the prescriptive or performance-based technical requirements.

For a pre-qualified measure, submit the application within 90 days after installation; for a performance-based project, apply at or before contracting and before demolition, removal, or installation begins.
Provide the signed application, recent utility bill, equipment specifications, contractor invoice, W-9, and any required savings calculations or supporting records.
Allow review or inspection and remain within current incentive limits and available program funds.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: National Fuel currently offers published 2026 prescriptive and performance-based incentives for qualifying Western New York business gas-efficiency projects. An eligible project following the correct timing and documentation path is likely to be approved; generic electric HVAC measures outside the gas program are not covered.
reviews.evidenceText: The 2026 nonresidential applications establish a 90-day post-installation route for pre-qualified measures and advance application before work for performance-based projects, with utility, invoice, specification, tax, and verification documentation.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible National Fuel residential natural-gas customer in Western New York and install the measure in an existing home.
Purchase and install new equipment that meets the current 2026 product and efficiency requirements; use a qualified contractor for required installations, including thermostats.
Complete eligible installations during the 2026 program year and submit the application by the published final filing deadline.
Provide the signed application, current utility bill, paid receipt or contractor invoice, manufacturer and model information, and any other measure-specific records.
Permit verification and remain within first-come funding and per-customer limits.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: National Fuel's current 2026 residential program provides rule-based rebates for qualifying gas HVAC, boiler, control, and related measures. A timely complete claim is likely to be paid while funds remain; the mapped battery-storage system is not a covered measure.
reviews.evidenceText: The current residential application covers qualifying 2026 installations for Western New York gas customers, requires contractor and purchase documentation, and sets a March 31, 2027 final filing date. Battery storage is not listed as an eligible rebate measure.

approvalRequirements: Maintain an eligible National Grid residential electric account in Massachusetts and the required online account access.
Use a compatible electric vehicle or supported connected Level 2 home charger and complete program enrollment.
Authorize and maintain the required vehicle or charger data connection and successfully complete device validation.
Charge the enrolled vehicle in Massachusetts during the defined off-peak periods and satisfy the initial participation period and ongoing program rules.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Charge Smart MA is an off-peak charging performance program that pays enrollment and usage credits after a compatible vehicle or charger is connected. It does not reimburse the capital cost of the mapped EV charger installation, so an installation award from this opportunity is unlikely.
reviews.evidenceText: The current program requires an eligible Massachusetts residential account, a compatible vehicle or connected charger, data enrollment, and off-peak charging behavior. Its payments are participation credits rather than charger-installation rebates.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible National Grid Massachusetts commercial, public, workplace, multifamily, or fleet applicant and use the correct current program segment.
Select charging hardware and network services from the applicable qualified lists and satisfy site, access, ownership, and technical requirements.
Submit a complete portal application with site plans, utility and load information, vendor estimates, funding disclosures, and other required project records.
Do not purchase equipment or begin construction before written preapproval, and return the signed Pre-Approval Offer Letter by the applicable 2026 deadline.
Complete the approved installation and submit invoices, activation records, closeout documents, and any required inspection or verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: National Grid is accepting new Massachusetts Public and Workplace applications on a first-come basis while funding remains and anticipates funding through 2026. A complete eligible project that receives preapproval and follows the offer-letter and closeout requirements is likely to receive the applicable infrastructure or charging-equipment incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: The current final-year program accepts new applications first-come while funds remain, requires qualified equipment and approval before purchase or construction, and requires a signed 2026 offer letter followed by project closeout and verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Rhode Island Energy commercial or industrial customer with a qualifying existing-building project.
Complete the applicable facility assessment, technical screening, or project scoping process and install measures that meet the approved 2026 program requirements.
Receive and sign an incentive offer or obtain project preapproval before installation when required, especially for custom or larger projects.
Submit the prescriptive application or final project records with invoices, specifications, savings information, and other requested documentation.
Permit pre- or post-installation inspection and final savings or installation verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Rhode Island Energy's approved 2026 commercial portfolio continues the large-business efficiency pathway for lighting, HVAC, motors, envelope, and custom projects. Qualifying projects are reviewed for eligibility and savings rather than competitively ranked, so an approved and completed project is likely to receive its calculated incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: The Rhode Island commission approved a 2026 energy-efficiency plan with active commercial retrofit, prescriptive, custom, assessment, offer-letter, invoice, and inspection pathways administered by Rhode Island Energy.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible National Grid Upstate New York business electric customer on a qualifying rate and complete the project at the served facility.
Select a measure still offered under the current program and satisfy its technical, contractor, and project requirements.
For electrification or custom work, engage National Grid early, complete any pre-inspection, and submit the scope and application before installation.
Sign the incentive Offer Letter or other required approval document before proceeding when the program requires a funding reservation.
Complete installation and submit final invoices, requested documents, and post-inspection or savings-verification records.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: National Grid continues active Upstate New York incentives for heat pumps, electrification, controls, envelope, custom, and other efficiency projects. A qualifying approved project is likely to receive its calculated incentive, although new lighting incentive commitments were phased out after 2025 and only legacy lighting projects can complete in 2026.
reviews.evidenceText: Current materials require early engagement, pre-inspection, engineering review, a signed offer letter, installation, final invoices, and post-inspection for electrification projects. They also state that new utility lighting incentives were phased out by December 31, 2025.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Rhode Island Energy residential customer and install the measure at the served home.
Use the applicable current 2026 rebate, instant-discount, assessment, or income-qualified pathway and satisfy its equipment and customer requirements.
Use a licensed, participating, or program-approved contractor where the selected HVAC, water-heating, or weatherization measure requires one.
Complete any required home energy assessment, income qualification, or advance authorization before work.
Submit the current form or contractor claim with invoices, model information, certificates, and any required verification or inspection records.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Rhode Island Energy's commission-approved 2026 residential portfolio maintains rule-based rebates, direct-install services, and assessment pathways for multiple mapped measures. A customer who uses the correct measure-specific channel and submits complete documentation is likely to receive the published benefit.
reviews.evidenceText: The approved 2026 Rhode Island plan continues residential HVAC, water-heating, appliance, weatherization, assessment, and income-qualified offerings. Current measure forms require customer, equipment, contractor, invoice, and verification documentation.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible National Grid Upstate New York residential electric customer and install the measure at the served home.
For a heat-pump project, use a participating NYS Clean Heat contractor and install equipment that meets the current sizing, efficiency, and application requirements.
Satisfy any existing-system decommissioning or project-tier condition required for the selected heat-pump incentive.
For a heat-pump water heater, use the current instant-discount or post-purchase rebate route and retain the required receipt, model, and installation documentation.
Allow contractor or program verification and comply with current customer, equipment, and funding limits.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: National Grid currently offers Upstate New York residential heat-pump incentives through participating contractors and a current heat-pump-water-heater rebate route. These are published, rule-based incentives, so a qualifying installation is likely to receive the applicable benefit after contractor or claim review.
reviews.evidenceText: Current National Grid pages direct heat-pump projects through participating NYS Clean Heat contractors and provide an active heat-pump-water-heater incentive with customer, equipment, purchase, and installation requirements.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible National Grid nonresidential natural-gas customer in the New York City service territory and complete the project at the served building.
Install a current qualifying high-efficiency gas, steam-system, control, or building-envelope measure that meets the applicable technical requirements.
Use the current online or measure-specific application and provide account, project, equipment, contractor, and cost information.
Obtain advance approval or an incentive offer before installation for custom, weatherization, or other projects when required.
Submit final paid invoices, specifications, completion records, and any required post-installation inspection or savings-verification documentation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: National Grid currently offers published Metro New York business gas-equipment and building-envelope incentives. Eligible natural-gas and weatherization projects that use the correct prescriptive or preapproved project route are likely to receive the applicable incentive after final documentation and verification; unrelated electric HVAC equipment is outside this gas program.
reviews.evidenceText: Current National Grid materials list qualifying business gas equipment, controls, steam measures, and envelope improvements and require the applicable application, project approval when specified, final invoices, and inspection or verification.
